To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) students in small colleges prefer teachers to researchers, and (2) female professors are less preferred than male professors.
the order of preference for the eight types of college professors is Teacher—Socialite (or Socializer)—Researcher—Administrator; and female professors are consistently less preferred to males.

(a) college students prefer a Teacher to a Socialite, a Researcher, or an Administrator; (b) female professors are less preferred than male professors; (c) college students do not distinguish between a Socialite and a Researcher; (d) college students prefer male professors more than female professors; and (e) college students do prefer male professors to female professors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social and psychological characteristics of the college instructor as perceived by students.
the social science professor's role in small colleges.
the student perceptions of four types of social scientists in small colleges and with the relationship between these perceptions and the sex of the professor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the order of preference for social science professors is Teacher—Socialite (Female)—Researcher—Administrator.
the order of preferential ranking of the four types of professors by small college students is Teacher—Socialite (male or female)—Researcher (male or female) —Administrator (male or female).
the college students of this study preferred the social science professor who was a teacher and socialite, and that they did not prefer the professor who was a researcher or administrator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

students prefer professors who are effective teachers, who are warm and friendly, who are interested in students, who are well informed about the field, who are interested and knowledgeable in research, and who are interested in the profession.
students' perceptions of professors in small colleges are more similar to those in universities than they were earlier thought to be.
the Teacher was preferred to the Socialite, who in turn was preferred to the Researcher and Administrator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
college students are more concerned about the quality of the instructor than about the professor's scholarly accomplishments.
college students in general are not particularly interested in professors who are administrators, and they are not particularly interested when professors are socialites.
the social science professor who is most preferred by students in small colleges is the one who is most like the students themselves, the teacher.
